h: Sheehan syndrome (postpartum pituitary failure): which hormone stays normal?
p: Aldosterone is driven by the renin-angiotensin system and hyperkalemia, not ACTH, so it is preserved. Failure to lactate (low prolactin), hypothyroid and adrenal symptoms follow pituitary infarction.

h: Inhaled 6-7 micron particles: main clearance route?
p: Roughly 2-10 micron particles deposit in the airways and are cleared by the mucociliary escalator; smaller particles reach alveoli and are taken up by macrophages; large ones are trapped in the nose.

h: Follicular lymphoma with BCL-2 overexpression: translocation?
p: t(14;18) places BCL2 under the IgH enhancer, blocking apoptosis. t(11;14) is mantle cell (cyclin D1); t(8;14) is Burkitt (MYC).

h: Fetus with CFTR Phe508 deletion: neonatal complication?
p: Cystic fibrosis (autosomal recessive, delta-F508) causes thick meconium and ileus in newborns; later pancreatic insufficiency and recurrent lung infections.

h: Germinal center: key B-cell event?
p: Germinal centers host somatic hypermutation, affinity maturation and class switching of B cells with T-follicular-helper help. Pro-B development is in marrow; double-positive T cells are in the thymus.

h: Adult with Down syndrome: new cyanosis, clubbing, high right heart pressures: syndrome?
p: An uncorrected left-to-right shunt (AV canal defect in Down syndrome) causes pulmonary hypertension, then shunt reversal to right-to-left with cyanosis and clubbing.

h: Fibular neck fracture: expected motor deficit?
p: The common peroneal nerve winds around the fibular neck; injury causes foot drop and loss of eversion, plus dorsal foot sensory loss. Plantarflexion (tibial nerve) is spared.

h: Ureter injured near the bladder: which pelvic surgery?
p: The ureter runs under the uterine artery ('water under the bridge') and can be clamped or ligated during hysterectomy, causing hydroureter and flank pain.

h: B-cell CD21 (complement receptor 2) is the receptor for which virus?
p: EBV gp350 binds CD21 on B cells (infectious mononucleosis, Burkitt lymphoma, post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease). HIV uses CD4 and CCR5/CXCR4.

h: Males with an X-linked recessive disease are called?
p: Males have one X, so a single mutant allele is fully expressed (full penetrance). Red-green color blindness is a classic X-linked recessive trait passed through carrier mothers.

h: Cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, red spots on mucosa, rash spreading downward: agent?
p: Measles: 3 C's (cough, coryza, conjunctivitis), Koplik spots, then a head-to-toe maculopapular rash. Give vitamin A; complications include SSPE and pneumonia.

h: Acute mania with chronic kidney disease: which mood stabilizer?
p: Lithium is renally cleared and nephrotoxic, so avoid it in renal impairment. Valproate is hepatically metabolized and antimanic; lamotrigine is not effective for acute mania.

h: Gluconeogenesis: enzyme converting fructose 1,6-bisphosphate to fructose 6-phosphate?
p: Gluconeogenesis bypasses three irreversible glycolytic steps with pyruvate carboxylase/PEPCK, fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase and glucose-6-phosphatase.

h: Infant stridor worse with feeding, relieved by neck extension, vomiting: diagnosis?
p: A vascular ring encircles the trachea and esophagus, causing stridor and dysphagia; barium swallow shows indentation. Laryngomalacia is typically better when prone.

h: Bortezomib: mechanism of action?
p: Blocking the proteasome causes ubiquitinated proteins to accumulate and triggers apoptosis; used in multiple myeloma and mantle cell lymphoma.

h: Polio with anterior horn destruction: reflex finding?
p: Anterior horn (lower motor neuron) loss gives flaccid weakness, atrophy, fasciculations and hyporeflexia. Babinski and pronator drift are upper motor neuron signs.

h: Tall man, gynecomastia, small firm testes, high LH/FSH: cytogenetic finding?
d: Absence of a second sex chromosome
p: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY): the extra X is inactivated as a Barr body. Primary hypogonadism gives high LH/FSH and low testosterone; infertility is common.

h: Odd dress, 'sixth sense' beliefs, social isolation, no frank psychosis: diagnosis?
p: Cluster A: odd beliefs, magical thinking and eccentric behavior without the sustained psychosis of schizophrenia.

h: Diltiazem: side effect to warn about?
p: Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers cause peripheral edema, constipation, bradycardia and AV block (avoid with beta-blockers).

h: Bethanechol for postoperative urinary retention: another use?
p: Bethanechol is a muscarinic agonist resistant to acetylcholinesterase; it stimulates detrusor and bowel motility. Edrophonium is used in myasthenia testing; pilocarpine for pupil/glaucoma.

h: IL-12 acting on a naive CD4 T cell: response?
p: IL-12 from macrophages and dendritic cells drives Th1 cells, which secrete IFN-gamma to activate macrophages against intracellular pathogens. Granzymes come from CD8 T and NK cells.

h: Rheumatoid arthritis: HLA association?
p: RA is associated with HLA-DR4 (shared epitope), anti-CCP antibodies and rheumatoid factor. HLA-B27 marks seronegative spondyloarthropathies; DQ2/DQ8 mark celiac disease.

h: Which mRNA codon change is a nonsense mutation?
p: Nonsense mutations convert an amino acid codon into a stop codon (UAA, UAG, UGA), giving a truncated protein. Here UAU (Tyr) becomes UAA (stop).

h: Ileal outpouching in a child, wall has all intestinal layers: diagnosis?
p: Meckel is a true diverticulum from persistent vitelline duct (rule of 2s), may contain ectopic gastric or pancreatic tissue, and causes bleeding or obstruction.

h: Pinpoint pupils and respiratory depression reversed by IV drug: receptor affected?
p: Naloxone is a competitive mu-opioid antagonist reversing opioid overdose; flumazenil acts at GABA-A for benzodiazepines.
